Subject: Re: Onboarding + invoice routing questions (Acme Logistics)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the form and sample CSV. Quick answers up front, then a short checklist so your ops team can make the adjustments:

High level recommendation
- Prefer portal for multi-entity suppliers: it gives us explicit entity selection on submission and eliminates parsing ambiguity.
- Email accepted as backstop, but we require a subject token to route correctly (see below).

Checklist / acceptance criteria (what we need before live ingestion)
1) Entity mapping: for portal -> please create two accounts in the onboarding form with exact display names and tax IDs. For email -> include a clear "Entity:" header line in the invoice PDF AND prefix in the filename (e.g., ACME-US_invoice_20250929.pdf).
2) PO stamping: PO number must be on the invoice PDF body (header or summary) and included as a metadata CSV column when available. If your system only stamps the PO on page 1 header that's OK — our OCR will pick it up but accuracy improves if the PO is on the first line of the invoice table.
3) Subject token (email fallback): when sending to ops@redwood-payables.com please prepend the subject with [RDW-ACME] followed by the supplier entity code. Example: "[RDW-ACME-US] Invoice 20250929 PO 12345". This token avoids manual routing.
4) Required fields: invoice number, invoice date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD), supplier entity code, PO number (if present), line-item CSV columns (qty, unit_price, line_total, tax_amount), currency.
5) VAT handling: include VAT_amount and VAT_registration columns in the CSV; for PDF invoices, please include a separate VAT line in the totals area with the VAT registration number on header.

Operational notes
- If you go portal: our ops team will configure entity IDs and send you a single sign-on invite; portal submission supports selecting the billing entity per upload.
- If you stick with email: we will provision a subject token for your account and share an email-to-queue address. Email ingestion has a 24–48 hour ack SLA and can create exceptions if PDFs are ambiguous.

Next steps for you
- Confirm which path you prefer (portal or email fallback) by EOD tomorrow.
- If portal: we will send the portal invite + acceptance test instructions. If email: we will email a token and sample subject line.

I attached our vendor intake playbook (vendor_intake_playbook.pdf) with examples. Looping Vanessa for the final operational details.

—Markus
Director, Vendor Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — operational follow-up from AP:

If vendor will be multi-entity (recommended portal):
- Create two vendor records in the onboarding form, one per legal entity. Each record must include: legal name, remittance address, tax ID/VAT, bank remit instructions (if split), and the preferred PO prefix.
- Portal submission supports selecting the target entity; once we receive the first test invoice we will validate mapping and confirm ledger codes.

If vendor stays with email fallback (accepted but limited):
- Use subject token exactly as Markus suggested: [RDW-ACME-<entity>]
- Filenames: <ENTITY>_<InvoiceNumber>_<YYYYMMDD>.pdf helps auto-match.
- For split payments we require a remittance line in the invoice that lists the split amounts and the corresponding ledger codes.

Minimum invoice fields we validate automatically (please ensure these are present):
- Invoice number (string)
- Invoice date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- PO number (if applicable)
- Supplier entity code (ACME-US or ACME-EU)
- Line items (description, qty, unit_price, tax)
- Total and tax breakdowns

Acknowledgements + SLA
- Portal: immediate success/failure ack (S/MIME style receipt) on upload.
- Email: ack within 24–48h; exceptions flagged for manual review.

I'll schedule a 30-min tech onboarding with your ops team if you'd like — we can walk through the portal UI and do a sample upload. Which timezone should I propose?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, AP Operations
Redwood Inference
